job.title: Plumber/Water Hygiene Technician
job.description:
Commercial Plumber / Water Hygiene Technician (Legionella Compliance) – Mobile Role – Glasgow – up to £35,000 DOE

An established facilities services company is seeking a Tierr 3 Water Hygiene Technician/Commercial plumber to join their team in a permanent, full-time mobile position. The role involves working across multiple locations throughout Glasgow and the wider Central Belt.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Working closely with the technical team, schedulers, and contract administrators to efficiently deliver planned preventative maintenance (PPM) and remedial water hygiene/treatment works.
  • Carrying out temperature monitoring, showerhead descaling, cold water storage tank inspections and cleans.
  • Completing cooling tower cleaning and disinfection works.
  • Servicing Thermostatic Mixing Valves (TMVs).
  • Conducting water sampling and analysis.
  • Performing LTHW system testing and analysis.
  • Dosing systems with inhibitor and biocide chemicals.
  • Undertaking cooling system testing and analysis.
  • Completing steam boiler testing and analysis.
  • Servicing water softeners and associated equipment.
  • Carrying out plumbing remedial works as required.
  • Ensuring all ACOP L8/site logbooks are accurate, compliant, and up to date when acting as Primary Technician.
Person Specification:

  • Qualified Plumber (Essential)
  • Legionella Awareness Training including knowledge of Regulations/Byelaws, L8 ACOP, HSG274 and any other relevant guidance
  • Knowledge of Water Hygiene service delivery requirements based on Table 2.1 HSG274 Part 2
  • Valid driving licence
  • This role includes a DBS Enhanced with Barred Lists therefore ability to pass is essential.
Salary & Benefits:

  • Competitive salary up to £35,000 depending on experience
  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
  • Option to purchase additional annual leave
  • Paid days for volunteering or community initiatives
  • Ongoing training and development, including professional qualifications and tailored learning support

job.description:

Exciting opportunity to work for a privately owned FM Service Provider situated in London. They will work closely with suppliers, subcontractors, and internal teams to ensure accurate and compliant estimates are incorporated into the final work package and tender submissions. The Estimator will be expected to work collaboratively with other parts of the business, facilitate handovers, finalise negotiations, and devise value engineering solutions. They will be expected to assist with supplier selection. The role will suit candidates who are agile and adaptable, experienced as an estimator within the commercial sector.

Hours of work

Monday to Friday (08:00am to 17:00pm)

Key duties & Responsibilities

  • Prepare and submit competitive tender packages, for a range of tender values up to £5m in accordance with the design, specification, and or scope of works available
  • To produce prime cost plans incorporating all elements of the scope, through discussions with clients
  • Send out trade specific enquires to suppliers and subcontractors to obtain competitive prices

  • Liaise closely with the other business streams to provide clear, robust, and competitive prices within joint bids
  • Produce estimates with transparency on itemised prime costs and applied markups, for review prior to submittal
  • Assist with the supply chain management & close out procedures

Requirements

  • Demonstrable experience as an Estimator with a reputable Contractor (Facilities Management, Property Management or Construction)
  • Demonstrable experience of costing tenders up to a value of c£5m
  • Strong experience in estimating (Essential)
  • Strong analytical, organisational, and communication skills
  • Ability to manage deadlines and produce highly accurate and clear tender submissions
  • Clear and confident written and verbal communication skills
  • Commercial and risk management aptitude, demonstrate the ability to manage multiple tenders at different stages, triaging tasks accordingly.
  • Strong presentation skills, with the ability to effectively create and deliver effective written reports and verbal presentations

Responsibilities
  • Setting strategy, policy and KPI's, identifying, justifying and implementing energy reduction projects and tools

  • Optimisation of HVAC and electrical plant and equipment whilst maintaining a statutory required service provision

  • Introduction of new technologies to support sustainability targets 
  • Manage energy budgets, deal with any energy specific bill recharges, and proactively lead on the correction of deviations against annual forecasts for consumption and billing

Requirements
  • Appropriate degree or equivalent knowledge and experience, ideally in a general sustainability, environmental, engineering, or building services discipline

job.title: Shifts Fabric Engineer
job.description:

CBW Staffing Solutions are looking for two experienced and qualified Fabric Engineers to join our client’s on-site facilities team based in Birmingham.

You’ll be responsible for carrying out reactive and planned maintenance across the building fabric, including general building repairs, plumbing and sanitaryware replacements, minor joinery, decoration and small-scale groundworks. You’ll also undertake repointing, paving repairs, fence maintenance and assist with office or desk moves when required.
This is a varied, hands-on role within a busy FMCG environment, ensuring the site remains safe, fully operational and well maintained.

We have two opportunities available, working a shift pattern of 4 on 4 off, 10am–10pm.

Package
  • Competitive salary of up to £40,000 per annum

  • 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays

  • Carry out reactive and planned building fabric maintenance and repairs
  • Perform general plumbing repairs and replace sanitaryware, including taps and toilet components
  • Complete basic groundworks and landscaping repairs, including repointing, paving and fence repairs
  • Undertake minor joinery, carpentry and decoration works
  • Support office moves and furniture relocations
  • Ensure the site remains safe, tidy and presentable

  • Flexible approach to working within a shift-based environment

The successful candidates will be mechanically biased (C&G / NVQ) with a proven track record in commercial building maintenance, ideally within a critical site (i.e. Bank, Data centre, Blue chip office etc).   • Respond to Service Desk reactive tasks as directed in accordance with SLAs

Undertake minor fabric maintenance works covering areas such as painting, furniture moving, etc and ensuring that any materials required to complete tasks are ordered in a timely and appropriate manner.

  • Lead and support internal and external audits, ensuring corrective actions are implemented promptly.

  • Manage team performance, including appraisals, training, development plans and competency records.

  • Work closely with the Service Desk and operational teams to coordinate resources and maintain service continuity.

  • Ensure local operating procedures, technical documentation and maintenance practices remain compliant with legislation and industry best practice.

  • Prepare operational, contract performance and energy management reports.

  • Monitor budgets, expenditure and financial forecasts, maintaining effective commercial control.

  • Participate in an out-of-hours on-call management rota as required.

  • Support organisational commitments to ethical standards, equality, diversity and inclusion.

Person Specification:

  • HNC/HND in Electrical Engineering or an equivalent discipline.
  • Recognised electrical qualifications and/or fully qualified electrician status.

  • Minimum of five years' post-qualification experience in a comparable technical services or contract management role.

  • Proven experience managing electrical and hard services within a contractual facilities management environment.

  • Strong leadership skills, with experience managing, motivating and developing engineering teams.

  • Excellent communication, organisation and stakeholder management skills.

  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and CAFM systems.

  • Full UK driving licence.

  • Ability to obtain the required Disclosure Scotland clearance, including PVG-level membership where applicable to the role.

  • Previous experience within healthcare facilities management or another critical operational environment.
  • Knowledge of healthcare technical standards, including SHTM 06-01, SHTM 06-02 and SHTM 06-03.

  • Experience or certification as an LV and/or HV Authorised or Approved Person.

  • Experience in a Responsible Person (RP) or Authorised Person (AP) capacity.

  • Knowledge of confined spaces, fire safety and lift management.

  • Experience managing projects and delivering engineering works within a live operational environment.

Salary & Benefits:

The successful candidate will receive a competitive remuneration package, with a basic salary of up to £55,000 per annum, plus additional allowances where applicable.

Financial package and allowances

  • Salary: Up to £55,000 per annum, depending on experience.

  • Responsibility allowance: £187.50 per month, subject to the relevant Responsible Person/Authorised Person appointment being approved by the appropriate Authorising Engineer and the applicable appointment criteria being met.

  • On-call allowance: £140 for participation in the on-call management rota. The applicable payment period and arrangements will be confirmed during the recruitment process.

Additional benefits

  • 25 days' annual leave plus public holidays.

  • Private healthcare cover for the employee.

  • Defined contribution pension scheme.

  • Life assurance worth twice your annual salary.

  • Company sick pay, increasing according to length of service.

  • Employee discounts across a wide range of major retailers and brands.

  • Discounted gym membership.

  • Cycle to Work scheme.

  • Holiday purchase scheme.

Hours of Work:

  • Monday to Friday.

  • 7.5 working hours per day, with a 30-minute unpaid break.

  • Flexible start and finish times between 07:00 and 17:00, subject to business requirements.

  • Participation in an out-of-hours on-call management rota.

Monday to Friday - 08:00am to 17:00pm

  • Review, assess and approve contractor RAMS prior to works commencing

  • Challenge and reject inadequate RAMS, ensuring appropriate amendments are made before authorisation
  • Monitor contractor activities to ensure works are undertaken in accordance with approved RAMS
  • Assist with the preparation and review of internal risk assessments and safe systems of work
  • Oversee the implementation and management of the site's Permit to Work (PTW) system
  • Ensure permits are correctly completed, authorised, monitored and closed out

  • Track outstanding statutory inspections, remedial actions and certification renewals
  • Liaise with engineering teams and specialist contractors to resolve outstanding compliance issues
  • Escalate overdue statutory tasks and significant compliance risks to the Engineering Management Team
  • Support compliance with relevant legislation, including the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act, Electricity at Work Regulations, COSHH and applicable building safety requirements
  • Ensure all contractors complete the required site inductions before commencing work
  • Monitor contractor performance against site health and safety standards
  • Ensure contractors follow agreed procedures, RAMS and permit requirements
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date compliance records, registers and certification
  • Produce weekly and monthly compliance reports for the Engineering Management Team and client.
Requirements

  • Electrically or Mechanically qualified (C&G, NVQ or apprenticeship)
  • Previous experience in a Compliance Supervisor, Compliance Coordinator, Health & Safety Supervisor or similar role within Facilities Management
  • Experience working within a commercial building, critical environment or multi-site FM contract
  • Strong knowledge of RAMS review and Permit to Work procedures
  • Experience conducting compliance audits and contractor inspections
  • Good understanding of statutory compliance requirements within building services maintenance.
  • Experience managing contractors and monitoring health and safety performance
  • Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail
  • Ability to identify compliance risks and implement corrective actions
  • NEBOSH General Certificate or equivalent health and safety qualification (Desirable)
  • IOSH Managing Safely  (Desirable)
  • Experience within a managing agent, property management or hard services FM environment.

job.title: ​Fit Out Supervisor
job.description:
Fit Out Supervisor - Client Direct / Property Management - Flagship Building - London (City) - Fixed Term Contract - Up to £67,500 + Bonus/Package

Exciting opportunity to work for an establish Property Manager company based in London. As the Fit-out Supervisor you will be a key experienced member of the property engineering team, carrying out duties as part of tenants and landlord fit-out, as directed by the engineering management team. You will coordinate between the tenant’s project team and M&E consultants. You will supervise a wide range of tasks on Landlord plant and equipment including electrical, mechanical, water treatment, domestic systems, cooling towers and HVAC plant. All work must be performed to the highest standard to ensure excellent service continues for tenants and building users. In return the company is offering a fixed term contract until August 2027, Up to £67,500, + Bonus/Package.

Hours of work

Monday to Friday - 08:00am to 17:30pm

Key duties & Responsibilities
  • Review contractor and tenant RAMS, issue and control permits to work.
  • Review and monitor access into landlord areas and plantrooms.
  • Maintain effective communication with the appointed fit out coordinator and M&E consultants.
  • Attend fit out meetings with the tenants, their contractors and fit out coordinator.
  • Monitor the tenant’s fit-out project, identifying any potential impacts to the base build infrastructure.
  • Undertake and supervise tasks as directed by the engineering management team and provide assistance to fit out coordinator, ensuring all work is carried out to required codes of practices and standards.
  • Verify commissioning and any integrations to base build systems, ensuring systems and O&M are updated.
  • Ensure the CAFM system is updated with sufficient information following any reactive tasks.
  • Carry out fault finding, diagnostics and rectification on HVAC systems, escalating where necessary.
  • Maintain effective communication with the shift and engineering management team including plant status, isolations, ongoing work and standards of housekeeping including risers.
  • Plant areas, workshops, stores and changing areas are kept to the highest standards of housekeeping.
  • Supervision and monitoring of contractors carrying out work and or fit out contractors.
  • Always uphold the integrity of the company and ensure the provision of high levels of customer services are provided.
  • Maintain effective reporting including critical plant status, plant isolations, issues arising, ongoing works, special task requests, and standard of housekeeping.
  • Ensure the accurate and timely completion of logbooks on completion of any related activities.
  • Ensure that specialist contractor service reports are signed off where necessary, that quality of work has been inspected, and faults/recommendations are escalated to the management team.
  • Escalate any defects and incidents immediately to engineering management.
  • Complete any site-specific system training as directed by your line manager.
  • Complete relevant Competent Persons Assessment within relevant discipline, within the agreed timeframe.
  • Ensure any parts required are clearly and accurately stated and any difficulties encountered with engineering activities are reported to the Engineering Management team.
  • Act as an Authorised Person as and when required, in accordance with the Company Safety Rules and Procedures.
  • Operation, diagnostics and fault finding for the following: HVAC plant – Pumps, motors, actuators, air handling units, pipework,fixtures and fittings, Public health systems and equipment – Taps, WHB, TMV’s, water
  • heaters, domestic hot and cold water, drainage systems, Boilers and Heating systems, Water treatment plant incl. cooling towers, Building Management and Energy Management Systems and Electrical systems and equipment.
Requirements
  • C&G, Level 3 or similar qualifications in electrical, mechanical or plumbing and heating.
  • IOSH Managing Safely
  • Proficient in the use of CAFM systems to complete reactive work orders
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Analytical mindset, able to interpret data to drive continuous improvement and service efficiency
  • Initiative to suggest and develop new ideas to increase efficiency and cost savings.
  • Ability to prioritise tasks to meet deadlines
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to deal with staff at all levels
  • Experience of supervising large engineering teams and or fit out teams
  • Able to commit to the FTC (August 2027)
Desirable
  • Experience of system modifications and minor installations
  • Project supervision of M&E fit-outs.
  • Awareness of the Tenant and landlord relationship within multi-occupied properties
  • Understanding of energy management systems and energy reduction initiatives
  • PASMA and IPAF qualifications
  • First aid training
  • Authorised Person in Electrical or Mechanical discipline

Monday to Friday – 08:00 to 17:00
